why: Three separate wrong conclusions were reached about a well-built tenant package in a single review, all from the same cause: the data was correct but nothing declared what it meant. An edge type pointed at a node type with no home dimension; a spend file's population was undeclared so it was compared against a differently-scoped file; a modelled subsidiary was nearly renamed because nothing declared it as an entity. A careful reader with full file access got all three wrong. A model with a retrieval window will do worse, faster, and with more confidence. This file is the missing declaration.

nodeTypes.label: Application or system
nodeTypes.note: A deployable application or platform the business uses.

nodeTypes.label: Organisational unit or accountable executive position
nodeTypes.note: Covers both the unit and the position accountable for it. Executive positions (CFO, CISO, CDAO) resolve here, NOT in workforce roles.

nodeTypes.label: Job family or persona
nodeTypes.note: A job family such as Pilot or Maintenance Technician. Deliberately distinct from org_unit: 'role' previously meant both, which left 1,039 edges pointing at a type with no home dimension.

nodeTypes.label: Interview or executive signal
nodeTypes.note: Interview evidence lives outside the active intake package, so endpoints cannot resolve against a canonical dimension. Reported, never silently accepted: an interview edge is proposed signal and may never be read as deterministic fact.

nodeTypes.label: Tower initiative
nodeTypes.note: Observed in graphs but resolving to no programme record. Declared here so the gap is reported as an unresolved endpoint rather than an unknown type. The fix is data: these initiatives belong in the programmes dimension.

nodeTypes.label: Contract or agreement
nodeTypes.note: Distinct from vendor: one vendor can hold several contracts, and renewal and commercial terms attach to the contract, not the supplier.

nodeTypes.label: Portfolio or operating company
nodeTypes.note: Holding-company tenants model their operating companies as graph nodes.

nodeTypes.label: Data domain
nodeTypes.note: Distinct from data_asset: a domain groups assets. Declared so the gap is reported rather than the type being unknown.

relationshipTypes.note: Technical accountability, which may differ from business accountability.
Interview edges are proposed signal. They may corroborate or contradict a source-system fact; they may never replace one.

filePopulationScope.why: Two files can both be correct and still not be comparable. Declaring the population each file represents is what stops a reader — human or model — summing across incompatible scopes and reporting a defect that does not exist.

declarations.example: IT application and platform spend only; excludes internal labour, facilities, telecom; full fiscal year; gross.
Enterprise-wide third-party contracts including non-IT categories such as ground handling and catering; contracted annual value, not in-year actual spend.

filePopulationScope.rule: A comparison across two files is only valid when both declare a population and the populations overlap. Absent a declaration, cross-file arithmetic is blocked, not estimated.

interviewClaimContract.why: Interview content is currently free text, so it can be quoted but not reconciled. A typed claim can be corroborated, contradicted, or left open — and that state is computable rather than editorial.
interviewClaimContract.rule: An interview claim may reach `attested` only through a named human attestation. It may never be promoted to deterministic fact by model inference.

segmentation.why: Without declared segmentation, 'what do we use for patient engagement?' forces a model to infer which of 500+ systems are patient-facing from their names. With a declared facet it is a filter. The same applies to 'what does the health plan spend on IT' or 'who owns care delivery'. Segmentation is what turns a flat inventory into something answerable.
segmentation.principle: Segmentation is declared once on the business function and inherited through relationships. A client is never asked to tag 500 systems by hand; they tag ~20 functions, and every system, KPI, contract, org unit and interview that connects to a function inherits its segments through the graph. Inheritance yields a SET, not a single value: a system supporting both care delivery and the patient portal is correctly both middle and front.

facets.label: Line of business
facets.note: Tenant-specific and must match how the client describes itself. Healthcare example: health plan; hospital / delivery network; medical group; post-acute; ancillary services. Airline example: mainline; regional; cargo; loyalty; MRO. Never inferred from a system name.

facets.label: Front / middle / back office

values.label: Customer engagement and experience
values.healthcare: Patient engagement and experience: access, scheduling, portal, contact centre, digital front door, member services
values.airline: Passenger engagement: booking, check-in, loyalty, disruption comms, contact centre

values.label: Core operating engine
values.healthcare: Clinical and care delivery: EHR, care management, utilisation management, claims adjudication, quality
values.airline: Flight, crew and airport operations, MRO, network planning

values.label: Enterprise support
values.healthcare: Finance, HR, supply chain, procurement, legal, corporate IT

facets.note: The three tiers are universal in structure; what belongs in each is industry-specific and is declared per industry, not guessed. Membership definitions live alongside 15_industry_context_patterns.csv.

inheritance.rule: A node with no directly declared facet value inherits the union of the facet values of every function it connects to. A node connected to no function has an UNDECLARED segment and must be reported, not defaulted.
inheritance.antiPattern: Do not default an unsegmented node to 'back office'. An undeclared segment is a gap to be surfaced; a defaulted one is a wrong answer that looks confident.

excludedFromPropagation.integrates_with: Symmetric and promiscuous. A shared integration bus touches everything, so propagating through it would hand almost every node every segment -- technically defensible, practically uninformative, and it would hide the nodes that genuinely have no segment.

inheritance.hopDistance: Segments propagate outward from functions up to 3 hops and the distance is written to `inherited_segment_hops`. A one-hop system supporting a function and a three-hop risk attached to its infrastructure are not the same strength of claim and must not look alike.

requiredContractColumns.note: These two columns on the ~20-row function dimension are the entire client ask. Everything else is derived. Adding them to the contract is the smallest change with the largest downstream effect in this whole model.

segmentation.whyThisMattersForRetrieval: A retrieval layer can filter on a declared facet but can only guess at an implied one. Segment-aware retrieval turns 'which systems serve the health plan's front office' from a semantic-similarity gamble into a deterministic subgraph selection, and makes the answer citable.

vocabularyOrigin: The first version of this ontology was derived from a single tenant's graph and then used to measure every other tenant. Six of seven 'failed'. That was an artifact of the sample, not evidence they were wrong: a survey of all seven found 32 node types and 40+ edge types in use, and most of the undeclared ones are plain synonyms of declared ones -- leader/owner/role all mean an accountable party, platform means infrastructure, ai_use_case means use_case. Rewriting six tenants to match one would have been a large migration justified by a sample of one. The vocabulary below is instead the union of what tenants actually express: synonyms are collapsed, and concepts that are genuinely distinct are declared rather than erased.

synonyms.why: A synonym is a different label for the same thing. Collapsing them at validation time costs nothing and rewrites no tenant data. A concept that is NOT a synonym must be declared as its own type instead -- collapsing a genuine distinction is how a model quietly loses information.
synonyms.note: Several synonyms are INVERSE relations, not direct renames. `uses` runs function->system while `supports` runs system->function; mapping one onto the other reverses the meaning and produces domain/range violations that look like data defects but are mapping errors. Each entry here was checked against the direction it is actually used in.
